doc.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Younger Detroiters: Louis Hayes, Curtis Fuller, Leon Henderson
summary: Hayes and Fuller were still schoolboys; Foster's peers were Harris, Flanagan and Burrell.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Louis Hayes, you said he was around Detroit? And then we’re going to figure out how you got from Detroit -- why did you join the Army? But Louis Hayes? Is there anything you want to say about him?
I didn’t know Louis Hayes well until after I’d gotten in Basie’s band.
So he was just another cat around?
Yeah, because he was very young. He was one of the young ones like Paul Chambers. I really wasn’t aware of him until --
So these cats were in high school?
But my generation was Barry, Tommy Flanagan, and Kenny Burrell. There were others that were older.
Was Joe or Leon -- was Leon Henderson around? Joe must have come later. Leon’s his brother -- Leon.
Yeah, they did come later. Leon, yeah.
